{'0': 'Apple has partnered with the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) to release a new guide aimed at helping families establish healthy digital habits.'}

{'1': 'The new guide follows the launch of several new child safety features in iOS 27.'}

{'2': 'According to Apple, the new guide is designed to help families strike a balance between screen time, sleep, exercise, schoolwork, and social interactions.'}

{'3': 'Apple noted that the guide offers families a six-step set of recommendations.'}

  • {'4': 'First, have a conversation about screen time, providing parents with tips on how to start the discussion and set expectations in a way that involves their children.'}
  • {'5': "Set up a child's account, enable age-based protections, and allow parents to manage their child's experience through parental controls."}
  • {'6': 'Configure safety settings for websites and apps, including Ask to Buy and Ask to Browse, so the whole family can review new apps and sites together.'}
  • {'7': 'Create a device usage schedule, using features like Time Allowances and Schedules to balance online time with sleep, homework, physical activity, and time with family and friends.'}
  • {'8': 'Manage communication features, letting parents decide who their children can contact; Communication Safety is enabled by default for all users under 18, helping protect children from viewing or sharing sensitive content.'}
  • {'9': 'Maintain ongoing conversations as children grow up, with guidance on adjusting the family plan.'}

{'10': "The new guide, titled *Building Healthy Digital Habits: A Guide for Families*, has been published on Apple's website."}
